english.notes:
(i) An offence under these Regulations may be tried by summary proceedings if in England and Wales, the information is laid before the end of the period of 12 months beginning on the day after the date on which evidence which the market surveillance authority thinks is sufficient to justify the proceedings comes to the market surveillance authority's knowledge.
(ii) For the purposes of paragraph (1) (a) a certificate signed by or on behalf of the prosecutor and stating the date on which such evidence came to the market surveillance authority's knowledge is to be conclusive evidence of that fact; and (b) a certificate stating that matter and purporting to be so signed is to be treated as so signed unless the contrary is proved. (Regulation 16).

other.penalty:
A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
An offence under these Regulations may be tried by summary proceedings if in England and Wales, the information is laid before the end of the period of 12 months beginning on the day after the date on which evidence which the market surveillance authority thinks is sufficient to justify the proceedings comes to the market surveillance authority's knowledge (Regulation 16 of the Ecodesign for Energy-Related Products Regulations 2010).

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
